name: One-shot backlog completeness audit v2

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  patch-and-validate:
    if: github.event.head_commit.message == 'Run backlog completeness audit v2'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Apply audited backlog improvements
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          from pathlib import Path

          def replace_one(text: str, old: str, new: str, label: str) -> str:
              count = text.count(old)
              if count != 1:
                  raise SystemExit(f"{label}: expected exactly one match, found {count}")
              return text.replace(old, new, 1)

          backlog_path = Path('BACKLOG.md')
          text = backlog_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')

          text = replace_one(
              text,
              'PR-33 through PR-47 cover complete Step 5 backtesting/evaluation and final Steps 1–5 sidecar parity.',
              'PR-33 through PR-47 cover complete Step 5 backtesting/evaluation and final Steps 1–5 sidecar parity. PR-48 through PR-49 cover deterministic final submission packaging and release validation.',
              'header PR range',
          )

          anchor = '''The backlog has been audited against the assignment brief, submission instructions, report template, and grading rubric. It is intentionally optimized for **two weak coding agents working in parallel**: PRs have explicit dependencies, fixed file ownership, deterministic interfaces, numbered tasks, and one-to-one matching acceptance criteria.\n\n---\n'''
          replacement = '''The backlog has been audited against the assignment brief, submission instructions, report template, and grading rubric. It is intentionally optimized for **two weak coding agents working in parallel**: PRs have explicit dependencies, fixed file ownership, deterministic interfaces, numbered tasks, and one-to-one matching acceptance criteria.\n\n## Global PR authoring contract\n\nThese rules apply to every implementation PR in this backlog and are deliberately strict so a weak coding agent does not have to infer intent.\n\n1. Every PR contains exactly one `Agent lane`, one explicit `Dependencies` line, one `Files owned` section, one numbered `Tasks` section and one numbered `Acceptance criteria` section.\n2. `Dependencies` names only lower-numbered PRs or explicitly declares `none`; prose-only dependencies such as “the Step 1 contract” are forbidden.\n3. Every task ID is `Txx.n` where `xx` is the PR number, task suffixes are contiguous from 1, and every task has exactly one acceptance criterion `ACxx.n` linking back to that exact task.\n4. A task describes one implementation responsibility. An acceptance criterion verifies the same responsibility with observable evidence; it must not introduce a new requirement absent from the task.\n5. `Files owned` is the complete write set for the PR. An agent must not edit a file outside that set. Generated artifacts committed by the PR are also listed explicitly.\n6. Parallel PRs in the published execution schedule must have disjoint write sets. If a newly discovered conflict exists, stop and serialize the PRs rather than resolving it ad hoc.\n7. Public function names, schemas, artifact paths, tie rules, numerical tolerances and model-selection rules are immutable once specified here unless a later backlog-audit PR explicitly changes the contract.\n8. Tasks must not use ambiguous phrases such as “as needed”, “relevant files”, “etc.” or “appropriate logic” when an exact behavior can be stated.\n9. Tests for source-code PRs are deterministic and offline unless the PR explicitly owns a live-data execution step.\n10. Notebook PRs are serialized. A notebook PR starts from the fully executed notebook on current `main`, executes it top-to-bottom, and commits stored outputs.\n11. Sidecar builders read canonical artifacts; they do not independently refit models, recreate state sequences or recompute an alternate analysis.\n12. If an agent cannot satisfy a task without changing an unowned file, changing a fixed interface, or making an unstated modeling choice, it must stop rather than guess.\n\nThe repository-level `scripts/check_backlog_contract.py` statically enforces PR numbering, required sections, explicit backward-only dependencies, contiguous task IDs, and one-to-one task/acceptance coverage.\n\n---\n'''
          text = replace_one(text, anchor, replacement, 'global PR contract insertion')

          dep_replacements = {
              '**Dependencies:** repository scaffold only': '**Dependencies:** none (current repository scaffold is the starting point)',
